observations: body L1-L23: the equation is added to the mean arc of visibility 11° 45′ when the difference is «decrescens», the arc of light being less than 12° 10′ (L3), and subtracted when it is «crescens» (L4); in the second method it is added to 10° 50′ when the difference belongs to 13° 40′, the arc of light being the smaller (L20-L21). A narrower crescent needs a longer arc of visibility, as in rule II of p. 268.

body L6, L24-L25, L29, L32, L37: «89,r.–v.» (L24) and «al–Ḥarrānī» (L25) have long dashes (5.3 and 5.6 pt); the dashes before «Altera» (L6) and before «Sectio» (L29, L32, L37) measure 10.0 to 10.3 pt.
body L15: the hyphen after «produ» prints as a blot, 2.0 by 2.6 pt.
body L26: «قومنا» is printed without the fatha that it has on p. 269, L25.
notes_left L1: note a) to chapter 41 ends on p. 266 with Thābit ibn Qurrah's death (288 H., 901) and his epistle on the visibility of the new moon.

notes_right L2: the formula has the form of the rule of the right spherical triangle, cos c = cos a cos b, with the arc of light as hypotenuse and the depression of the Sun and the distance of the Moon from the foot of the perpendicular as sides. With sines and cosines to the radius R, as in the formula of p. 269, L5, it reads cos dist. = R cos arcus lucis : cos depress. Solis; the print sets R in the denominator, which divides the right side by R²; kept as printed.
